reflection.text:
Scored correct - Protein degradation (ALLN). Verdict correct=true via protocol 1-NN majority vote, 4/4 wells, summed similarity 2.33.

What the evidence got right:
- compare_to_reference_atlas was decisive despite early morphological ambiguity. e5 was already 2/2 Protein degradation (k-neighbours: DNA replication 3/10, Protein degradation 2/10, Protein synthesis 2/10 - i.e. nearest-neighbour vote already separated from k-neighbour spread) and e9 went to 4/4 Protein degradation (k-neighbours: DNA replication 3/10, Protein degradation 2/10, Microtubule destabilizers 2/10). Per-well similarities in unblinding confirm a dose escalation: 0.318 at 1 uM w_799403842a (weak, near threshold), 0.564 at 3 uM w_b9bba7558b, 0.757 at 10 uM w_daa103d348, 0.692 at 30 uM w_6824fff027. I weighted this correctly in e16 (0.68) over microscopist calls.
- Dose-response trends captured the transition that review noted as 3-to-10 uM. e14 tub_mean rho=+1.0 p=0, e11 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80, e12 frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80, e13 cell_count rho=-0.80, e15 nuc_solidity rho=-0.80. Absolute well phenotypes were consistent: e3 at 30 uM tub_glcm_contrast z=+42.5 nuc_solidity z=-25.3, e6 at 10 uM nuc_solidity z=-23.7 tub_glcm_contrast +21.9 act_std +10.8, e7 at 3 uM nuc_major_axis +15.2 nuc_area +9.8, e2 at 1 uM nuc_dna_mean -9.5 nuc_solidity -5.0 frac_mitotic_like -3.8. e10 nuc_area rho=+0.20 p=0.8 correctly argued against a simple polyploid-area increase despite e7.
- update_hypotheses e16 appropriately left Aurora (0.12), Microtubule stabilizer (0.08), Eg5 (0.04) as explainers of morphology but not of atlas vote, with rationale that tub increase and multinucleation can be secondary to proteasome block. This is plausible in this screening context - proteasome inhibition via bortezomib-type mechanisms can manifest as mitotic catastrophe/cell cycle arrest and mitotic arrest interactions, consistent with PMID 28055975, PMID 28416751 and PMID 38992067, without needing a direct microtubule target.

What misled / what I missed:
- describe_phenotype e4 (density lower, 9 obs: unknown, Microtubule stabilizers, Eg5, Aurora) and e8 (density similar, 12 obs: Aurora) - classical composite microscopy limitation noted in review: it cannot separate stabilizer vs destabilizer vs Aurora/Eg5 rosettes. I did not overrule them, but they explain why p=0.68 not higher was calibrated.
- k-neighbour lists e5/e9 retained DNA replication / Protein synthesis / Microtubule destabilizer signals that could have supported alternative hypotheses if NSC vote were split. I did not acquire a low-dose well (0.03-0.3 uM range in e1) to define onset, and all 4 wells were rep1 only, so the weak 1 uM vote (0.318) was not replicated. e14 p=0 is artifactual with n=4 monotonic; all other dose_response p=0.2 or 0.8, i.e. trends not statistically significant with 4 points - I treated rho magnitude as suggestive, which review allowed given budget_left=0.
- e2 frac_mitotic_like z=-3.8 at 1 uM is actually *depleted* mitotic-like, while e13/e12 imply loss of cells and gain of multinucleate proxy at high dose. I did not resolve this inversion - consistent with proteasome block causing delayed mitotic slippage/multinucleation rather than classic mitotic arrest accumulation, but I had no phospho-H3 / live timing to prove it.
- lookup_compound e18/e19 returned no curated mechanisms and a structural mismatch: name CID 6915732 vs BBBC021 structure CID 21118339. I submitted on atlas vote alone without orthogonal target engagement. Conclusion proposed proteasome activity assay/ubiquitin blot/FACS + phospho-H3/tubulin grayscale - that is what a real follow-up still needs. search_literature e21 0 hits for "MG132 mitotic arrest multinucleation" vs e22 90 hits for broader proteasome inhibition mitotic arrest illustrates query sensitivity; I should not have expected a perfect literature match for the secondary phenotype.

Acquisition choices:
- Sampling 1,3,10,30 uM bracketed the phenotypic switch and satisfied protocol dose bracket despite using only 4 of 8 doses. No second replicate was affordable; concordance across 3 higher-dose wells mitigated single-replicate risk but leaves identity mismatch unresolved.

- Dose-response trends captured the transition that review noted as 3-to-10 uM. e14 tub_mean rho=+1.0 p=0, e11 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80, e12 frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80, e13 cell_count rho=-0.80, e15 nuc_solidity rho=-0.80. Absolute well phenotypes were consistent: e3 at 30 uM tub_glcm_contrast z=+42.5 nuc_solidity z=-25.3, e6 at 10 uM nuc_solidity z=-23.7 tub_glcm_contrast +21.9 act_std +10.8, e7 at 3 uM nuc_major_axis +15.2 nuc_area +9.8, e2 at 1 uM nuc_dna_mean -9.5 nuc_solidity -5.0 frac_mitotic_like -3.8. e10 nuc_area rho=+0.20 p=0.8 correctly argued against a simple polyploid-area increase despite e7.
- update_hypotheses e16 appropriately left Aurora (0.12), Microtubule stabilizer (0.08), Eg5 (0.04) as explainers of morphology but not of atlas vote, with rationale that tub increase and multinucleation can be secondary to proteasome block. This is plausible in this screening context - proteasome inhibition via bortezomib-type mechanisms can manifest as mitotic catastrophe/cell cycle arrest and mitotic arrest interactions, consistent with PMID 28055975, PMID 28416751 and PMID 38992067, without needing a direct microtubule target.

What misled / what I missed:
- describe_phenotype e4 (density lower, 9 obs: unknown, Microtubule stabilizers, Eg5, Aurora) and e8 (density similar, 12 obs: Aurora) - classical composite microscopy limitation noted in review: it cannot separate stabilizer vs destabilizer vs Aurora/Eg5 rosettes. I did not overrule them, but they explain why p=0.68 not higher was calibrated.
- k-neighbour lists e5/e9 retained DNA replication / Protein synthesis / Microtubule destabilizer signals that could have supported alternative hypotheses if NSC vote were split. I did not acquire a low-dose well (0.03-0.3 uM range in e1) to define onset, and all 4 wells were rep1 only, so the weak 1 uM vote (0.318) was not replicated. e14 p=0 is artifactual with n=4 monotonic; all other dose_response p=0.2 or 0.8, i.e. trends not statistically significant with 4 points - I treated rho magnitude as suggestive, which review allowed given budget_left=0.
- e2 frac_mitotic_like z=-3.8 at 1 uM is actually *depleted* mitotic-like, while e13/e12 imply loss of cells and gain of multinucleate proxy at high dose. I did not resolve this inversion - consistent with proteasome block causing delayed mitotic slippage/multinucleation rather than classic mitotic arrest accumulation, but I had no phospho-H3 / live timing to prove it.
- lookup_compound e18/e19 returned no curated mechanisms and a structural mismatch: name CID 6915732 vs BBBC021 structure CID 21118339. I submitted on atlas vote alone without orthogonal target engagement. Conclusion proposed proteasome activity assay/ubiquitin blot/FACS + phospho-H3/tubulin grayscale - that is what a real follow-up still needs. search_literature e21 0 hits for "MG132 mitotic arrest multinucleation" vs e22 90 hits for broader proteasome inhibition mitotic arrest illustrates query sensitivity; I should not have expected a perfect literature match for the secondary phenotype.

Acquisition choices:
- Sampling 1,3,10,30 uM bracketed the phenotypic switch and satisfied protocol dose bracket despite using only 4 of 8 doses. No second replicate was affordable; concordance across 3 higher-dose wells mitigated single-replicate risk but leaves identity mismatch unresolved.

What was right:
- NSC 4/4 Protein degradation e9 after 2/2 e5, with monotonic similarity 0.318->0.564->0.757->0.692
- dose_response e11 e12 e13 e14 e15 consistent with irregular nuclei and tubulin accumulation/multinucleation secondary to proteostasis block
- e16 correctly down-weighted microscopist Aurora/Eg5/stabilizer e4 e8

What was wrong or missed:
- e4 e8 morphology mimicked microtubule/Aurora due to known overlap - required citation that proteasome inhibition can cause mitotic catastrophe/arrest PMID 28055975 PMID 28416751 PMID 38992067
- all wells rep1, weak low-dose vote, p-values 0.2-0.8 not significant, no low-dose 0.03-0.3 uM sampled
- identity_check mismatch e18 e19 not resolved before submission

Proposed next experiment: Re-acquire low doses 0.1-1 uM in duplicate plus 10 uM duplicate; run proteasome-Glo + K48-ubiquitin western + DNA content FACS and phospho-H3 vs DMSO and reference proteasome inhibitor, to decouple tubulin/multinucleate secondary effects from primary proteasome block and resolve CID mismatch by LC-MS of stock.
